blending_nodes::BlendModeNode.description: Applies the blend mode to the input graphics. Setting this allows for customizing how overlapping content is composited together.

Blend Mode.description: The choice of equation that controls how brightness and color blends between overlapping pixels.

Content.description: The content that will be composited when rendering.

blending_nodes::BlendModeNode.name: node.type.blending_nodes.blendmodenode

blending_nodes::ClippingMaskNode.description: Sets whether the input graphics inherit the alpha of the content beneath them, "clipping" them to that content.

Clip.description: Whether the content inherits the alpha of the content beneath it.

Content.description: The content that will be composited when rendering.

blending_nodes::ClippingMaskNode.name: node.type.blending_nodes.clippingmasknode

blending_nodes::OpacityNode.description:
Modifies the opacity and/or fill of the input graphics by multiplying the existing values by these percentages.
Opacity affects the transparency of the content (together with anything above which is clipped to it).
Fill affects the transparency of the content itself, independent of any content clipped to it.

Content.description: The content that will be composited when rendering.

Fill.description:
How visible the content should be, independent of any content clipped to it.
Ranges from 0% (fully transparent) to the default of 100% (fully opaque).

Has Fill.description: Whether the *Fill* property is enabled, multiplying the existing fill by the chosen percentage.

Has Opacity.description: Whether the *Opacity* property is enabled, multiplying the existing opacity by the chosen percentage.

Opacity.description:
How visible the content should be, including any content clipped to it.
Ranges from the default of 100% (fully opaque) to 0% (fully transparent).

blending_nodes::OpacityNode.name: node.type.blending_nodes.opacitynode

core_types::vector::AsVectorNode.description: Type-asserts a value to be vector data.
core_types::vector::AsVectorNode.name: node.type.core_types.vector.asvectornode

core_types::vector::AutoTangentsNode.description: Automatically constructs tangents (Bézier handles) for anchor points in a vector path.

Preserve Existing.description: If active, existing non-zero handles won't be affected.

Spread.description: The amount of spread for the auto-tangents, from 0 (sharp corner) to 1 (full spread).

core_types::vector::AutoTangentsNode.name: node.type.core_types.vector.autotangentsnode

Content.description: Artwork to be copied and placed at each point.

Random Rotation.description: Range of randomized angles given to each placed copy, in degrees ranging from furthest clockwise to counterclockwise.

Random Rotation Seed.description: Seed to determine unique variations on all the randomized copy angles.

Random Scale Bias.description: Bias for the probability distribution of randomized sizes (0 is uniform, negatives favor more of small sizes, positives favor more of large sizes).

Random Scale Max.description: Maximum range of randomized sizes given to each placed copy.

Random Scale Min.description: Minimum range of randomized sizes given to each placed copy.

Random Scale Seed.description: Seed to determine unique variations on all the randomized copy sizes.

core_types::vector::CutSegmentsNode.description: Cuts path segments into separate disconnected pieces where each is a distinct subpath.
core_types::vector::CutSegmentsNode.name: node.type.core_types.vector.cutsegmentsnode

core_types::vector::DecimateNode.description: Decimates vector paths into polylines by sampling any curves into line segments, then removing points that don't significantly contribute to the shape using the Ramer-Douglas-Peucker algorithm.

Content.description: The vector paths to decimate.

Tolerance.description: The maximum distance a point can deviate from the simplified path before it is kept.

core_types::vector::DecimateNode.name: node.type.core_types.vector.decimatenode

core_types::vector::ExtractTransformNode.description: Obtains the transform of the input content.
core_types::vector::ExtractTransformNode.name: node.type.core_types.vector.extracttransformnode

core_types::vector::JitterPointsNode.description: Perturbs the positions of anchor points in vector geometry by random amounts and directions.

Along Normals.description: Whether to offset anchor points along their normal direction (perpendicular to the path) or in a random direction. Free-floating and branching points have no normal direction, so they receive a random-angled offset regardless of this setting.

Content.description: The vector geometry with points to be jittered.

Max Distance.description: The maximum extent of the random distance each point can be offset.

Seed.description: Seed used to determine unique variations on all randomized offsets.

core_types::vector::JitterPointsNode.name: node.type.core_types.vector.jitterpointsnode

core_types::vector::MorphNode.description:
Interpolates the geometry, appearance, and transform between multiple vector layers, producing a single morphed vector shape.

*Progression* morphs through all objects. Interpolation is linear unless *Path* geometry is provided to control the trajectory between key objects. The **Origins to Polyline** node may be used to create a path with anchor points corresponding to each object. Other nodes can modify its path segments.

Content.description: The vector objects to interpolate between. Mixed graphic content is deeply flattened to keep only vector elements.

Distribution.description:
The parameter of change that influences the interpolation speed between each object. Equal slices in this parameter correspond to the rate of progression through the morph. This must be set to a parameter that changes.

"Objects" morphs through each group element at an equal rate. "Distances" keeps constant speed with time between objects proportional to their distances. "Angles" keeps constant rotational speed. "Sizes" keeps constant shrink/growth speed. "Slants" keeps constant shearing angle speed.

Path.description: An optional control path whose anchor points correspond to each object. Curved segments between points will shape the morph trajectory instead of traveling straight. If there is a break between path segments, the separate subpaths are selected by index from the integer part of the progression value. For example, `[1, 2)` morphs along the segments of the second subpath, and so on.

Progression.description: The fractional part `[0, 1)` traverses the morph uniformly along the path. If the control path has multiple subpaths, each added integer selects the next subpath.

Reverse.description: Swap the direction of the progression between objects or along the control path.

core_types::vector::MorphNode.name: node.type.core_types.vector.morphnode

core_types::vector::OffsetPointsNode.description:
Displaces anchor points along their normal direction (perpendicular to the path) by a set distance.
Points with 0 or 3+ segment connections have no well-defined normal and are left in place.

Content.description: The vector geometry with points to be offset.

Distance.description: The distance to offset each anchor point along its normal. Positive values move outward, negative values move inward.

core_types::vector::OffsetPointsNode.name: node.type.core_types.vector.offsetpointsnode

core_types::vector::PathIsClosedNode.description: Determines if the subpath at the given index is closed, meaning its ends are connected together forming a loop.

Content.description: The vector content whose subpaths are inspected.

Index.description: The index of the subpath to check, counting across the element's subpaths.

core_types::vector::PathIsClosedNode.name: node.type.core_types.vector.pathisclosednode

core_types::vector::PointsToPolylineNode.description: Creates a polyline from a series of vector points, replacing any existing segments that may already exist.
core_types::vector::PointsToPolylineNode.name: node.type.core_types.vector.pointstopolylinenode

core_types::vector::ReadIndexNode.description:
Produces the index of the current iteration of a loop by reading from the evaluation context, which is supplied by downstream nodes such as *Repeat*.

Nested loops can enable 2D or higher-dimensional iteration by using the *Loop Level* parameter to read the index from outer levels of loops.

Loop Level.description:
The number of nested loops to traverse outwards (from the innermost loop) to get the index from. The most upstream loop is level 0, and downstream loops add levels.

In programming terms: inside the double loop `i { j { ... } }`, *Loop Level* 0 = `j` and 1 = `i`. After inserting a third loop `k { ... }`, inside it, levels would be 0 = `k`, 1 = `j`, and 2 = `i`.

core_types::vector::ReadIndexNode.name: node.type.core_types.vector.readindexnode

Loop Level.description:
The number of nested loops to traverse outwards (from the innermost loop) to get the position from. The most upstream loop is level 0, and downstream loops add levels.

In programming terms: inside the double loop `i { j { ... } }`, *Loop Level* 0 = `j` and 1 = `i`. After inserting a third loop `k { ... }`, inside it, levels would be 0 = `k`, 1 = `j`, and 2 = `i`.

core_types::vector::RelaxPointsNode.description: Evens out the distances between points by applying Lloyd's relaxation, moving every interior point toward the center of its Voronoi cell.

Iterations.description: The number of relaxation steps to apply. A fractional value runs the whole steps and then blends partway toward one more step, so the amount of relaxation can be animated smoothly.

Source.description: A vector path or point cloud to relax.

core_types::vector::RelaxPointsNode.name: node.type.core_types.vector.relaxpointsnode

core_types::vector::SamplePolylineNode.description: Convert vector geometry into a polyline composed of evenly spaced points.
core_types::vector::SamplePolylineNode.name: node.type.core_types.vector.samplepolylinenode

core_types::vector::SimplifyNode.description: Simplifies vector paths by reducing the number of curve segments while preserving the overall shape within the given tolerance.

Content.description: The vector paths to simplify.

Tolerance.description: The maximum distance the simplified path may deviate from the original.

core_types::vector::SimplifyNode.name: node.type.core_types.vector.simplifynode

core_types::vector::TriangulateNode.description:
Builds a Delaunay triangulation connecting the anchor points. It is the geometric dual of the **Voronoi** node: a mesh of triangles in which no point lies inside any triangle's circumscribed circle.

When Connect Cells is off, every triangle becomes its own closed, fillable subpath. When on, the triangles share their common points and segments, forming a single connected mesh.
core_types::vector::TriangulateNode.name: node.type.core_types.vector.triangulatenode

core_types::vector::VoronoiCellsNode.description:
Builds a Voronoi diagram from the anchor points. Each point claims the region of space closest to it, and those regions tessellate the plane. Cells around the outside are clipped to the convex hull of the points so the diagram stays finite.

When Connect Cells is off, every cell becomes its own closed, fillable subpath. When on, the cells share their common points and segments, forming a single connected mesh.
core_types::vector::VoronoiCellsNode.name: node.type.core_types.vector.voronoicellsnode

graphene_core::animation::AnimationTimeN.description: Produces the time, in seconds on the timeline, since the beginning of animation playback.
graphene_core::animation::AnimationTimeN.name: node.type.graphene_core.animation.animationtimenode

graphene_core::animation::PointerPositio.description: Produces the current position of the user's pointer within the document canvas.

graphene_core::animation::RealTimeNode.description: Produces a chosen representation of the current real time and date (in UTC) based on the system clock.

graphene_core::animation::RealTimeNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.animation.realtimenode

graphene_core::context::ReadNumberNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.context.readnumbernode

graphene_core::context_modification::Con.description:

Features To Keep.description: The parts of the context to keep when evaluating the input value. All other parts are nullified.

Value.description: The data to pass through, evaluated with the stripped down context.

graphene_core::context_modification::Con.name: node.type.graphene_core.context_modification.contextmodificationnode

graphene_core::memo::MemoizeNode.description:
Helps speed up repeated renders in a computationally-heavy part of the node graph.

graphene_core::memo::MemoizeNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.memo.memoizenode

graphene_core::memo::MonitorNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.memo.monitornode

graphene_core::ops::BundleNode.description: Wraps a whole `List` onto the wire as one rank-0 `Item<Bundle<T>>` so an entire collection can feed a connector that carries it as one opaque cell.
graphene_core::ops::BundleNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.ops.bundlenode

graphene_core::ops::ConvertItemNode.description: The [`Convert`]-based counterpart of `into_item`, casting an `Item` wire's element to a connector's numeric element type.
graphene_core::ops::ConvertItemNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.ops.convertitemnode

graphene_core::ops::ConvertListNode.description: The `List` counterpart of `convert_item`, casting every element to the connector's numeric element type.
graphene_core::ops::ConvertListNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.ops.convertlistnode

graphene_core::ops::EmbedItemNode.description:
Moves a whole `Item` wire inside an element type like `Graphic` that embeds ranked values as its variants.

graphene_core::ops::EmbedItemNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.ops.embeditemnode

graphene_core::ops::EmbedListNode.description: The `List` counterpart of `embed_item`, each item moving whole inside its own embedding element.
graphene_core::ops::EmbedListNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.ops.embedlistnode

graphene_core::ops::IntoItemNode.description:
Converts an `Item` wire's element to a different element type it can produce through the std `Into` trait,

graphene_core::ops::IntoItemNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.ops.intoitemnode

graphene_core::ops::IntoListNode.description: The `List` counterpart of `into_item`, converting every element to a different element type it can produce.
graphene_core::ops::IntoListNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.ops.intolistnode

graphene_core::ops::IntoNode.description: Shifts a whole wire value onto a connector's type through the std `Into` trait, serving the whole-`List` erasure onto `ListDyn` under the input adapter identifier.

graphene_core::ops::ItemToAttributeValue.description: Boxes a ranked wire's element into a type-erased attribute value, carrying the cell's attributes through the wire.
graphene_core::ops::ItemToAttributeValue.name: node.type.graphene_core.ops.itemtoattributevaluenode

graphene_core::ops::ListToAttributeValue.name: node.type.graphene_core.ops.listtoattributevaluenode

graphene_core::ops::PassthroughNode.description: Passes-through the input value without changing it. This is useful for rerouting wires for organization purposes.
graphene_core::ops::PassthroughNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.ops.passthroughnode

graphene_core::ops::UnbundleNode.description: Unwraps a `Bundle` wire back into the whole `List` it carries, restoring the collection after it passed through a connector as one opaque cell.
graphene_core::ops::UnbundleNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.ops.unbundlenode

graphene_core::vector::AssignColorsNode.description: Uniquely sets the fill and/or stroke style of every vector element to individual colors sampled along a chosen gradient.

Content.description: The content with vector paths to apply the fill and/or stroke style to.

Gradient.description: The range of colors to select from.

Randomize.description: Whether to randomize the color selection for each element from throughout the gradient.

Repeat Every.description: The number of elements to span across the gradient before repeating. A 0 value will span the entire gradient once.

Seed.description:
The seed used for randomization.
Seed to determine unique variations on the randomized color selection.

graphene_core::vector::AssignColorsNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.vector.assigncolorsnode

graphene_core::vector::CombinePathsNode.description: Combines every vector path across the input into a single compound path.
graphene_core::vector::CombinePathsNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.vector.combinepathsnode

graphene_core::vector::CutPathNode.description:
Cuts a path at a given progression from 0 to 1 along the path, creating two new subpaths from the original one (if the path is initially open) or one open subpath (if the path is initially closed).

If multiple subpaths make up the path, the whole number part of the progression value selects the subpath and the decimal part determines the position along it.

Content.description: The path to insert a cut into.

Parameterized Distance.description: Traverse the path using each segment's Bézier curve parameterization instead of the Euclidean distance. Faster to compute but doesn't respect actual distances.

Progression.description: The factor from the start to the end of the path, 0–1 for one subpath, 1–2 for a second subpath, and so on.

Reverse.description: Swap the direction of the path.

graphene_core::vector::CutPathNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.vector.cutpathnode

graphene_core::vector::DashPatternNode.description: Builds a stroke dash pattern from a list of lengths that alternate between dash and gap, starting with a dash.

Lengths.description: The dash and gap lengths, alternating and starting with a dash.

graphene_core::vector::DashPatternNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.vector.dashpatternnode

graphene_core::vector::FillNode.description: Applies a fill style to the vector content, giving an appearance to the area within the interior of the geometry.

Content.description: The content with vector paths to apply the fill style to.

graphene_core::vector::FillNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.vector.fillnode

graphene_core::vector::IndexPointsNode.description:
Retrieves the vec2 position (in local space) of the anchor point at the specified index within a vector element.
If no value exists at that index, the position (0, 0) is returned.

Content.description: The vector element containing the anchor points to be retrieved.

Index.description: The index of the points to retrieve, starting from 0 for the first point. Negative indices count backwards from the end, starting from -1 for the last point.

graphene_core::vector::IndexPointsNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.vector.indexpointsnode

graphene_core::vector::PositionOnPathNod.description:
Determines the position of a point on the path, given by its progression from 0 to 1 along the path.

If multiple subpaths make up the path, the whole number part of the progression value selects the subpath and the decimal part determines the position along it.

Content.description: The path to traverse.

Parameterized Distance.description: Traverse the path using each segment's Bézier curve parameterization instead of the Euclidean distance. Faster to compute but doesn't respect actual distances.

Progression.description: The factor from the start to the end of the path, 0–1 for one subpath, 1–2 for a second subpath, and so on.

Reverse.description: Swap the direction of the path.

graphene_core::vector::PositionOnPathNod.name: node.type.graphene_core.vector.positiononpathnode

graphene_core::vector::StrokeNode.description: Applies a stroke style to the vector content, giving an appearance to the area within the outline of the geometry.

Align.description: The alignment of stroke to the path's centerline or (for closed shapes) the inside or outside of the shape.

Cap.description: The shape of the stroke at open endpoints.

Content.description: The content with vector paths to apply the stroke style to.

Dash Offset.description: The phase offset distance from the starting point of the dash pattern.

Dash Pattern.description: The stroke dash pattern. Each length forms a distance in a pattern where the first length is a dash, the second is a gap, and so on. If the list is an odd length, the pattern repeats with solid-gap roles reversed.

Join.description: The curvature of the bent stroke at sharp corners.

Miter Limit.description: The threshold for when a miter-joined stroke is converted to a bevel-joined stroke when a sharp angle becomes pointier than this ratio.

graphene_core::vector::StrokeNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.vector.strokenode

graphene_core::vector::TangentOnPathNode.description:
Determines the angle of the tangent at a point on the path, given by its progression from 0 to 1 along the path.

If multiple subpaths make up the path, the whole number part of the progression value selects the subpath and the decimal part determines the position along it.

Content.description: The path to traverse.

Parameterized Distance.description: Traverse the path using each segment's Bézier curve parameterization instead of the Euclidean distance. Faster to compute but doesn't respect actual distances.

Progression.description: The factor from the start to the end of the path, 0–1 for one subpath, 1–2 for a second subpath, and so on.

Radians.description: Whether the resulting angle should be given in as radians instead of degrees.

Reverse.description: Swap the direction of the path.

graphene_core::vector::TangentOnPathNode.name: node.type.graphene_core.vector.tangentonpathnode

graphene_std::platform_application_io::U.name: node.type.graphene_std.platform_application_io.uploadtexturenode

graphene_std::text::TextNode.description:
Produces a styled text string carrying all typographic attributes.

Use the **Text to Vector** node to convert this into vector geometry if desired.

Align.description: The horizontal alignment of each line of text within its surrounding box. To have an effect on a single line of text, *Max Width* must be set.

Font.description: The loaded font file used to draw the text. The editor resolves the chosen typeface to these bytes via the resource system.

Has Max Height.description: Whether the *Max Height* property is enabled so that lines beyond it are not drawn.

Has Max Width.description: Enables the maximum width constraint so lines can wrap.

Letter Spacing.description: Additional spacing, in pixels, added between each character.

Letter Tilt.description: The angle of faux italic slant applied to each glyph.

Line Height.description:
The line height ratio, relative to the font size. Each line is drawn lower than its previous line by the distance of *Size* × *Line Height*.

0 means all lines overlap. 1 means all lines are spaced by just the font size. 1.2 is a common default for readable text. 2 means double-spaced text.

Max Height.description: The maximum height that the text block can occupy. Excess lines are not drawn.

Max Width.description: The maximum width that the text block can occupy before wrapping to a new line. Otherwise, lines do not wrap.

Size.description: The font size used to draw the text.

Text.description: The text content to be drawn.

graphene_std::text::TextNode.name: node.type.graphene_std.text.textnode

List.description: The list of data to filter.

graphic_nodes::graphic::FilterNode.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.filternode

graphic_nodes::graphic::FlattenColorNode.description: Converts a `Graphic[]` into a `Color[]` by deeply flattening any color content it contains, and discarding any non-color content.
graphic_nodes::graphic::FlattenColorNode.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.flattencolornode

graphic_nodes::graphic::FlattenGradientN.description: Converts a `Graphic[]` into a `Gradient[]` by deeply flattening any gradient content it contains, and discarding any non-gradient content.
graphic_nodes::graphic::FlattenGradientN.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.flattengradientnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::FlattenGraphicNo.description: Removes a level of nesting from a `Graphic[]`, or all nesting if "Fully Flatten" is enabled.
graphic_nodes::graphic::FlattenGraphicNo.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.flattengraphicnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::FlattenRasterNod.description: Converts a `Graphic[]` into a `Raster[]` by deeply flattening any raster content it contains, and discarding any non-raster content.
graphic_nodes::graphic::FlattenRasterNod.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.flattenrasternode

graphic_nodes::graphic::FlattenVectorNod.description: Converts a `Graphic[]` into a `Vector[]` by deeply flattening any vector content it contains, and discarding any non-vector content.
graphic_nodes::graphic::FlattenVectorNod.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.flattenvectornode

graphic_nodes::graphic::GradientToColors.description: Unwraps a gradient into a `Color[]` of its stops, keeping any `position` and `midpoint` attributes that place them along the ramp. Attributes belonging to the gradient as a whole (like spread and interpolation), rather than its individual color stops, are not preserved.
graphic_nodes::graphic::GradientToColors.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.gradienttocolorsnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::IntoGroupNode.description:
Nests the input graphical content in a wrapper graphic, collecting it all into a single group.
The inverse of this node is 'Flatten Graphic'.
graphic_nodes::graphic::IntoGroupNode.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.intogroupnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ItemAtIndexNode.description:
Returns the item at the specified index in a list, keeping its attributes.
If no value exists at that index, the element type's default is returned.

Index.description: The index of the item to retrieve, starting from 0 for the first item. Negative indices count backwards from the end of the list, starting from -1 for the last item.

List.description: The list of data to take the item from.

graphic_nodes::graphic::ItemAtIndexNode.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.itematindexnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::LegacyLayerExten.description:
Performs an obsolete function as part of a migration from an older document format.
Users are advised to delete this node and replace it with a new one.
graphic_nodes::graphic::LegacyLayerExten.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.legacylayerextendnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ListIndicesNode.description: Counts out the index of each item in a list (0, 1, 2, and so on), producing a list of numbers with one for each item.

List.description: The list whose items are counted.

Start Index.description: The number that the count begins from for the first item.

graphic_nodes::graphic::ListIndicesNode.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.listindicesnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ListSliceNode.description:
Extracts a portion of a list, starting at "Start" and ending before "End".

Negative indices count from the end of the list. If the index of "Start" equals or exceeds "End", the result is an empty list.

End.description: The index the portion ends before, which is not included. Zero or negative indices count from the end of the list.

List.description: The list of data to take a portion of.

Start.description: The index of the first item in the portion. Negative indices count from the end of the list.

graphic_nodes::graphic::ListSliceNode.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.listslicenode

graphic_nodes::graphic::NumberSequenceNo.description: Generates a list of evenly spaced numbers, starting at a value and progressing by a step (which may be positive, negative, or zero) for a given count.

Start.description: The first number in the sequence.

Step.description: The amount added to reach each successive number.

graphic_nodes::graphic::NumberSequenceNo.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.numbersequencenode

graphic_nodes::graphic::PathOfSubgraphNo.description:
Returns the path identifying the subgraph (network) that contains this proto node — i.e. the input `node_path`
with its own trailing entry dropped. The terminating element of the returned path is the document node whose
encapsulated network we live in, so the path doubles as a unique reference to that node at any nesting depth.
Used as the value source for stamping the `editor:layer_path` attribute on each item of a layer's output, which lets
editor tools (e.g. selection, click target routing) trace data back to its owning layer regardless of whether
the layer is at the root document network or nested inside a custom subgraph.
graphic_nodes::graphic::PathOfSubgraphNo.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.pathofsubgraphnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeArt.description: Reads a named `Artboard` attribute from the input list, outputting each value as an element of a new `Artboard[]`.
graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeArt.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.readattributeartboardnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeBle.description: Reads a named `BlendMode` attribute from the input list, outputting each value as an element of a new `BlendMode[]`.
graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeBle.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.readattributeblendmodenode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeBoo.description: Reads a named `bool` attribute from the input list, outputting each value as an element of a new `bool[]`.
graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeBoo.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.readattributeboolnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeCol.description: Reads a named `Color` attribute from the input list, outputting each value as an element of a new `Color[]`.
graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeCol.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.readattributecolornode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeGra.description: Reads a named `GradientForm` attribute from the input list, outputting each value as an element of a new `GradientForm[]`.
graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeGra.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.readattributegradientformnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeGra.description: Reads a named `GradientHueDirection` attribute from the input list, outputting each value as an element of a new `GradientHueDirection[]`.
graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeGra.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.readattributegradienthuedirectionnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeGra.description: Reads a named `GradientInterpolation` attribute from the input list, outputting each value as an element of a new `GradientInterpolation[]`.
graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeGra.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.readattributegradientinterpolationnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeGra.description: Reads a named `GradientSpace` attribute from the input list, outputting each value as an element of a new `GradientSpace[]`.
graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeGra.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.readattributegradientspacenode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeGra.description: Reads a named `GradientSpread` attribute from the input list, outputting each value as an element of a new `GradientSpread[]`.
graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeGra.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.readattributegradientspreadnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeGra.description: Reads a named `Gradient` attribute from the input list, outputting each value as an element of a new `Gradient[]`.
graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeGra.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.readattributegradientstopsnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeNum.description: Reads a named numeric attribute (`f64`, `u64`, or `u32`) from the input list, outputting each value as an element of a new `f64[]`. Integer values are converted to `f64`.
graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeNum.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.readattributenumbernode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeRas.description: Reads a named `Raster` attribute from the input list, outputting each value as an element of a new `Raster[]`.
graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeRas.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.readattributerasternode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeStr.description: Reads a named `String` attribute from the input list, outputting each value as an element of a new `String[]`.
graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeStr.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.readattributestringnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeTra.description: Reads a named `DAffine2` transform attribute from the input list, outputting each value as an element of a new `DAffine2[]`.
graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeTra.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.readattributetransformnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeVec.description: Reads a named `Vector` attribute from the input list, outputting each value as an element of a new `Vector[]`.
graphic_nodes::graphic::ReadAttributeVec.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.readattributevectornode

graphic_nodes::graphic::RemoveAtIndexNod.description:
Returns the list with the item at the specified index removed.
If no value exists at that index, the list is returned unchanged.

Index.description: The index of the item to remove, starting from 0 for the first item. Negative indices count backwards from the end of the list, starting from -1 for the last item.

graphic_nodes::graphic::RemoveAtIndexNod.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.removeatindexnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ReverseNode.description: Reverses the order of the items in a list, so the last item comes first and the first comes last.

List.description: The list of data to reverse.

graphic_nodes::graphic::ReverseNode.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.reversenode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ShiftNode.description: Shifts the items in a list by a number of positions. With wrapping, items pushed off one end reappear at the other. Otherwise they are dropped, shortening the list.

Amount.description: How many positions to shift each item. Positive values shift items toward the start of the list, negative toward the end.

List.description: The list of data to shift.

Wrap.description: Whether items shifted off one end wrap around to the other. When off, they are dropped and the list gets shorter.

graphic_nodes::graphic::ShiftNode.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.shiftnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::ShuffleNode.description: Randomly reorders the items in a list. The same seed always produces the same ordering.

List.description: The list to have its items randomly reordered.

Seed.description: Seed to determine the unique variation of the random shuffle ordering. The same seed always produces the same ordering.

graphic_nodes::graphic::ShuffleNode.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.shufflenode

graphic_nodes::graphic::SortNode.description: Reorders a list's items from smallest to largest, either by each item's own value or by a parallel list of sortable values in the *Sort Order* input. The sort is stable, so items with the same sort order retain their relative positions.

List.description: The list of data to reorder.

Reverse.description: Reverses the sorted list order, following descending order instead of ascending (numbers largest-to-smallest, strings Z-to-A, etc.).

Sort Order.description: The optional list of orderable values, corresponding item-to-item with the input list, to sort by instead of the items' own values.

graphic_nodes::graphic::SortNode.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.sortnode

graphic_nodes::graphic::WriteAttributeNo.description:
Sets a named attribute on the input list, computing one value per item via the value-producing input. That input
is evaluated once per item, with the item's index and the item itself (as a list containing only that item,
passed as a vararg) provided via context, so the upstream pipeline can return a different value per item that may
be derived from the item's own data. If the attribute already exists, its values are replaced; if not, it's added.
The value is type-erased into an `Item<AttributeValueDyn>` by the auto-inserted input adapter, so this node only
monomorphizes over `T` instead of the cartesian product `(T, U)`.

Content.description: The list to set the named attribute on (one value per item).

Name.description: The attribute name (key) to write or replace.

Value.description: The node that produces the attribute value for each item. Called once per item with the item's index in context.

graphic_nodes::graphic::WriteAttributeNo.name: node.type.graphic_nodes.graphic.writeattributenode

math_nodes::AbsoluteValueNode.description:
The absolute value function (`abs`) removes the negative sign from an input value, if present.

With a vec2 input, this applies separately to the X and Y components. For the overall length of a vec2, see the "Magnitude" node instead.

Value.description: The number to be made positive.

math_nodes::AbsoluteValueNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.absolutevaluenode

math_nodes::AddNode.description: The addition operation (`+`) calculates the sum of two scalar numbers or vec2s.

Addend.description: The right-hand side of the addition operation.

Augend.description: The left-hand side of the addition operation.

math_nodes::AddNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.addnode

math_nodes::AllNode.description: Outputs true only if every value in the input list is true. An empty list gives true.
math_nodes::AllNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.allnode

math_nodes::AngleBetweenNode.description:
Calculates the angle swept between two vec2s.

The angle ranges from -180° to 180° (or -π to π radians) and its sign gives the sweep direction from the "Direction From" input to the "Direction To" input: positive for clockwise, negative for counterclockwise, as drawn in the viewport and matching the direction convention of the Transform node's rotation.

Direction From.description: The direction the angle is measured from.

Direction To.description: The direction the angle is measured to.

Radians.description: Whether the resulting angle should be given in radians instead of degrees.

math_nodes::AngleBetweenNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.anglebetweennode

math_nodes::AngleToNode.description: Calculates the angle needed for a rightward-facing object placed at the "Position From" point to turn so it points toward the "Position To" point.

Position From.description: The position from which the angle is measured.

Position To.description: The position toward which the angle is measured.

Radians.description: Whether the resulting angle should be given in radians instead of degrees.

math_nodes::AngleToNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.angletonode

math_nodes::AnyNode.description: Outputs true if at least one value in the input list is true. An empty list gives false.
math_nodes::AnyNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.anynode

math_nodes::AsF64Node.description: Convert an integer to a decimal number of the type f64, which may be the required type for certain node inputs.
math_nodes::AsF64Node.name: node.type.math_nodes.asf64node

math_nodes::AsU32Node.description: Convert a number to an integer of the type u32, which may be the required type for certain node inputs.
math_nodes::AsU32Node.name: node.type.math_nodes.asu32node

math_nodes::AsU64Node.description: Convert a number to an integer of the type u64, which may be the required type for certain node inputs.
math_nodes::AsU64Node.name: node.type.math_nodes.asu64node

math_nodes::AverageNode.description: Averages all the numbers in the input list. An empty list gives 0.
math_nodes::AverageNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.averagenode

math_nodes::BoolValueNode.description: Constructs a bool value which may be set to true or false.
math_nodes::BoolValueNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.boolvaluenode

math_nodes::CeilingNode.description:
The ceiling function (`ceil`) rounds up an input value to the nearest whole number, unless the input number is already whole.

With a vec2 input, this applies separately to the X and Y components.

Value.description: The number to be rounded up.

math_nodes::CeilingNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.ceilingnode

math_nodes::ClampNode.description:
The clamp function (`clamp`) restricts a number to a specified range between a minimum and maximum value. The minimum and maximum values are automatically swapped if they are reversed.

With vec2 inputs, this applies separately to the X and Y components.

Max.description: The right (greater) side of the range. The output is never greater than this number.

Min.description: The left (smaller) side of the range. The output is never less than this number.

Value.description: The number to be clamped, which is restricted to the range between the minimum and maximum values.

math_nodes::ClampNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.clampnode

math_nodes::ColorValueNode.description: Constructs a color value which may be set to any color.
math_nodes::ColorValueNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.colorvaluenode

math_nodes::CombineVec2Node.description:
Composes a vec2 from its X and Y components.

The inverse of this node is **Split Vec2**, which decomposes a vec2 back into its X and Y components.

X.description: The X component of the vec2.

Y.description: The Y component of the vec2.

math_nodes::CombineVec2Node.name: node.type.math_nodes.combinevec2node

math_nodes::CosineInverseNode.description: The inverse cosine trigonometric function (`acos`) calculates the angle whose cosine is the input value.

Radians.description: Whether the resulting angle should be given in as radians instead of degrees.

Value.description: The given value for which the angle is calculated. Must be in the domain `[-1, 1]` (it will be clamped to -1 or 1 otherwise).

math_nodes::CosineInverseNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.cosineinversenode

math_nodes::CosineNode.description:
The cosine trigonometric function (`cos`) calculates the ratio of the angle's adjacent side length to its hypotenuse length.

With a vec2 input, this applies separately to the X and Y components.

Radians.description: Whether the given angle should be interpreted as radians instead of degrees.

math_nodes::CosineNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.cosinenode

math_nodes::CrossProductNode.description:
The cross product operation (`×`) calculates the signed area of the parallelogram formed by a vec2 pair.

The sign gives the rotation direction from the first vec2 to the second: positive for clockwise, negative for counterclockwise, and 0 when both are parallel, as drawn in the viewport.

Other Value.description: The vec2 on the right-hand side of the cross product operation.

Value.description: The vec2 on the left-hand side of the cross product operation.

math_nodes::CrossProductNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.crossproductnode

math_nodes::DistanceNode.description: Measures the distance between two points, which is the length of the straight line segment connecting them.

Position From.description: The point the distance is measured from.

Position To.description: The point the distance is measured to.

math_nodes::DistanceNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.distancenode

math_nodes::DivideNode.description:
The division operation (`÷`) calculates the quotient of two scalar numbers or vec2s.

Produces 0 for any division by 0. With vec2 inputs, this applies separately to the X and Y components.

Denominator.description: The right-hand side of the division operation.

Numerator.description: The left-hand side of the division operation.

math_nodes::DivideNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.dividenode

math_nodes::DotProductNode.description:
The dot product operation (`·`) calculates the degree of similarity of a vec2 pair based on their angles and lengths.

Calculated as `‖a‖‖b‖cos(θ)`, it represents the product of their lengths (`‖a‖‖b‖`) scaled by the alignment of their directions (`cos(θ)`).
The output ranges from the positive to negative product of their lengths based on when they are pointing in the same or opposite directions.
If either vec2 has zero length, the output is 0.

Normalize.description: Whether to normalize both input vec2s so the calculation ranges in `[-1, 1]` by considering only their degree of directional alignment.

Other Value.description: The other operand of the dot product operation.

Value.description: An operand of the dot product operation.

math_nodes::DotProductNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.dotproductnode

math_nodes::EqualsNode.description: The equality operation (`==`, `XNOR`) compares two values and returns true if they are equal, or false if they are not.

Other Value.description: The other of the two values to compare for equality.

Value.description: One of the two values to compare for equality.

math_nodes::EqualsNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.equalsnode

math_nodes::EvaluateGradientNode.description: Evaluates the color at the specified position along the gradient, given a position from 0 (left) to 1 (right). Positions beyond that range follow the gradient's `gradient_spread` attribute: Pad (default), Reflect, Repeat, or Clear. Colors between stops interpolate in the gradient's `gradient_space` color space.
math_nodes::EvaluateGradientNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.evaluategradientnode

math_nodes::ExponentNode.description:
The exponent operation (`^`) calculates the result of raising a number to a power.

With vec2 inputs, this applies separately to the X and Y components.

Base.description: The base number that is raised to the power.

Power.description: The power to which the base number is raised.

math_nodes::ExponentNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.exponentnode

math_nodes::FloorNode.description:
The floor function (`floor`) rounds down an input value to the nearest whole number, unless the input number is already whole.

With a vec2 input, this applies separately to the X and Y components.

Value.description: The number to be rounded down.

math_nodes::FloorNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.floornode

math_nodes::FootprintValueNode.description: Constructs a footprint value which may be set to any transformation of a unit square describing a render area, and a render resolution at least 1x1 integer pixels.
math_nodes::FootprintValueNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.footprintvaluenode

math_nodes::GradientCyclicNode.description: Sets whether each gradient in the input list treats its stops as a cycle, interpolating from the last stop back around to the first.
math_nodes::GradientCyclicNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.gradientcyclicnode

math_nodes::GradientFormNode.description: Sets the form (linear or radial) of each gradient in the input list.
math_nodes::GradientFormNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.gradientformnode

math_nodes::GradientHueDirectionNode.description: Sets which way around the hue wheel each gradient in the input list interpolates, for polar color spaces.
math_nodes::GradientHueDirectionNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.gradienthuedirectionnode

math_nodes::GradientInterpolationNode.description: Sets the path each gradient in the input list interpolates along, deciding whether it jumps, turns corners, or flows smoothly through its stops.
math_nodes::GradientInterpolationNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.gradientinterpolationnode

math_nodes::GradientMidpointsNode.description:
Skews how rapidly the color flows across each interval between color stops, bunching up the transition toward one end instead of progressing uniformly. Each value places the halfway color within its corresponding interval, measured as a fraction of the distance (0 to 1) between the adjacent stops. A 0.5 midpoint keeps a uniform transition rate through the interval.

Non-cyclic gradients have no interval following the last stop, meaning the midpoint is ignored in that position.

A list shorter than the stop count repeats its last value, a longer list is truncated, and an empty list sets each midpoint to its default of 0.5.
math_nodes::GradientMidpointsNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.gradientmidpointsnode

math_nodes::GradientPositionsNode.description:
Sets the position of each of a gradient's stops, a factor from 0 to 1 along the gradient.

A list shorter than the stop count repeats its last value, a longer list is truncated, and an empty list sets each stop to its default evenly spaced position.
math_nodes::GradientPositionsNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.gradientpositionsnode

math_nodes::GradientReverseNode.description: Reverses the order of each gradient's stops, moving the color at the start of the ramp to the end and vice versa.
math_nodes::GradientReverseNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.gradientreversenode

math_nodes::GradientShiftNode.description:
Shifts every stop along each gradient's ramp, sliding the colors within the gradient without moving the gradient itself.

The fraction is measured against the whole ramp. A cyclic gradient spins, wrapping past the end back around to the start so 1 is a full turn that lands where it began. A gradient that isn't cyclic has no loop to spin around, so its stops slide off the end and keep going, leaving the visible ramp to blend between whichever colors still span it.
math_nodes::GradientShiftNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.gradientshiftnode

math_nodes::GradientSpaceNode.description: Sets the color space in which each gradient in the input list interpolates between its stops.
math_nodes::GradientSpaceNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.gradientspacenode

math_nodes::GradientSpreadNode.description: Sets how each gradient in the input list extends past its endpoints: Pad, Reflect, Repeat, or Clear.
math_nodes::GradientSpreadNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.gradientspreadnode

math_nodes::GradientStretchNode.description:
Stretches or squeezes the spacing of each gradient's stops around a pivot, spreading the colors within the gradient without moving the gradient itself.

The factor multiplies every stop's distance from the pivot, so 2 spreads the ramp over twice its span while 0.5 packs it into half. A negative factor mirrors the stops across the pivot, reversing the order of the colors.

The pivot is the one point that stays put, measured against the whole ramp from 0 at the start to 1 at the end.
math_nodes::GradientStretchNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.gradientstretchnode

math_nodes::GradientValueNode.description: Constructs a gradient value which may be set to any sequence of color stops to represent the transition between colors.
math_nodes::GradientValueNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.gradientvaluenode

math_nodes::GreaterThanNode.description:
The greater-than operation (`>`) compares two values and returns true if the first value is greater than the second, or false if it is not.
If enabled with *Or Equal*, the greater-than-or-equal operation (`>=`) is used instead.

Or Equal.description: Uses the greater-than-or-equal operation (`>=`) instead of the greater-than operation (`>`).

Other Value.description: The number on the right-hand side of the comparison.

Value.description: The number on the left-hand side of the comparison.

math_nodes::GreaterThanNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.greaterthannode

math_nodes::GreatestCommonDivisorNode.description: The greatest common divisor (GCD) calculates the largest positive integer that divides both of the two input numbers without leaving a remainder.

Other Value.description: The other of the two numbers for which the GCD is calculated.

Value.description: One of the two numbers for which the GCD is calculated.

math_nodes::GreatestCommonDivisorNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.greatestcommondivisornode

math_nodes::HslaToColorNode.description: Constructs a color value from hue, saturation, lightness, and alpha components given as numbers from 0 to 1.
math_nodes::HslaToColorNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.hslatocolornode

math_nodes::HsvaToColorNode.description: Constructs a color value from hue, saturation, value, and alpha components given as numbers from 0 to 1.
math_nodes::HsvaToColorNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.hsvatocolornode

math_nodes::LeastCommonMultipleNode.description: The least common multiple (LCM) calculates the smallest positive integer that is a multiple of both of the two input numbers.

Other Value.description: The other of the two numbers for which the LCM is calculated.

Value.description: One of the two numbers for which the LCM is calculated.

math_nodes::LeastCommonMultipleNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.leastcommonmultiplenode

math_nodes::LerpNode.description:
Linearly interpolates between the start and end values, where a factor of 0 gives the start value, 1 gives the end value, and 0.5 gives their midpoint.

With vec2 inputs, this traces the straight line path between the two points.

Clamped.description: Whether to constrain the factor within 0 to 1, preventing extrapolation beyond the start and end values.

End.description: The value produced when the factor is 1.

Factor.description: The mix between the start (at 0) and end (at 1) values.

Start.description: The value produced when the factor is 0.

math_nodes::LerpNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.lerpnode

math_nodes::LessThanNode.description:
The less-than operation (`<`) compares two values and returns true if the first value is less than the second, or false if it is not.
If enabled with *Or Equal*, the less-than-or-equal operation (`<=`) is used instead.

Or Equal.description: Uses the less-than-or-equal operation (`<=`) instead of the less-than operation (`<`).

Other Value.description: The number on the right-hand side of the comparison.

Value.description: The number on the left-hand side of the comparison.

math_nodes::LessThanNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.lessthannode

math_nodes::LogarithmNode.description:
The logarithmic function (`log`) calculates the logarithm of a number with a specified base. If the natural logarithm function (`ln`) is desired, set the base to "e".

With vec2 inputs, this applies separately to the X and Y components.

Base.description: The base of the logarithm, such as 2 (binary), 10 (decimal), and e (natural logarithm).

math_nodes::LogicalAndNode.description: The logical AND operation (`&&`) returns true if both of the two inputs are true, or false if any are false.

math_nodes::LogicalAndNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.logicalandnode

math_nodes::LogicalNotNode.description: The logical NOT operation (`!`) reverses true and false value of the input.

math_nodes::LogicalNotNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.logicalnotnode

math_nodes::LogicalOrNode.description: The logical OR operation (`||`) returns true if either of the two inputs are true, or false if both are false.

Other Value.description: The other of the two boolean values, either of which may be true for the node to output true.

Value.description: One of the two boolean values, either of which may be true for the node to output true.

math_nodes::LogicalOrNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.logicalornode

math_nodes::MagnitudeNode.description: The magnitude operator (`‖x‖`) calculates the length of a vec2, which is the distance from the base to the tip of the arrow it represents.
math_nodes::MagnitudeNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.magnitudenode

math_nodes::MathNode.description: Calculates a mathematical expression with input values "A" and "B".

Expression.description: A math expression that may incorporate "A" and/or "B", such as `sqrt(A + B) - B^2`.

Operand A.description: The value of "A" when calculating the expression.

Operand B.description: The value of "B" when calculating the expression.

math_nodes::MathNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.mathnode

math_nodes::MaxNode.description:
The maximum function (`max`) picks the larger of two numbers.

With vec2 inputs, this applies separately to the X and Y components.

Other Value.description: The other of the two numbers, of which the greater is returned.

Value.description: One of the two numbers, of which the greater is returned.

math_nodes::MaxNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.maxnode

math_nodes::MaximumNode.description: Gives the largest number in the input list. An empty list gives 0.
math_nodes::MaximumNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.maximumnode

math_nodes::MinNode.description:
The minimum function (`min`) picks the smaller of two numbers.

With vec2 inputs, this applies separately to the X and Y components.

Other Value.description: The other of the two numbers, of which the lesser is returned.

Value.description: One of the two numbers, of which the lesser is returned.

math_nodes::MinNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.minnode

math_nodes::MinimumNode.description: Gives the smallest number in the input list. An empty list gives 0.
math_nodes::MinimumNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.minimumnode

math_nodes::ModuloNode.description:
The modulo operation (`%`) calculates the remainder from the division of two scalar numbers or vec2s.

The sign of the result shares the sign of the numerator unless *Always Positive* is enabled.

Always Positive.description: Ensures the result is always positive, even if the numerator is negative.

Modulus.description: The right-hand side of the modulo operation.

Numerator.description: The left-hand side of the modulo operation.

math_nodes::ModuloNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.modulonode

math_nodes::MultiplyNode.description: The multiplication operation (`×`) calculates the product of two scalar numbers, vec2s, or transforms.

Multiplicand.description: The right-hand side of the multiplication operation.

Multiplier.description: The left-hand side of the multiplication operation.

math_nodes::MultiplyNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.multiplynode

math_nodes::NormalizeNode.description:
Scales the input vec2 to unit length while preserving its direction. This is equivalent to dividing the input vec2 by its own magnitude.

Returns 0 when the input vec2 has zero length.
math_nodes::NormalizeNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.normalizenode

math_nodes::NotEqualsNode.description: The inequality operation (`!=`, `XOR`) compares two values and returns true if they are not equal, or false if they are.

Other Value.description: The other of the two values to compare for inequality.

Value.description: One of the two values to compare for inequality.

math_nodes::NotEqualsNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.notequalsnode

math_nodes::NumberValueNode.description: Constructs a number value which may be set to any real number.
math_nodes::NumberValueNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.numbervaluenode

math_nodes::PercentageValueNode.description: Constructs a number value which may be set to any value from 0% to 100% by dragging the slider.
math_nodes::PercentageValueNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.percentagevaluenode

math_nodes::RandomNode.description: The random function (`rand`) converts a seed into a random number within the specified range, inclusive of the minimum and exclusive of the maximum. The minimum and maximum values are automatically swapped if they are reversed.

Max.description: The larger end of the range within which the random number is generated.

Min.description: The smaller end of the range within which the random number is generated.

Seed.description: Seed to determine the unique variation of which number is generated.

math_nodes::RandomNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.randomnode

math_nodes::ReciprocalNode.description:
The reciprocal operation (`1/x`) calculates the multiplicative inverse of a number.

Produces 0 if the input is 0. With a vec2 input, this applies separately to the X and Y components.

Value.description: The number for which the reciprocal is calculated.

math_nodes::ReciprocalNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.reciprocalnode

math_nodes::RemapNode.description:
Linearly maps an input value from one range to another. The ranges may be reversed.

For example, 0.5 in the input range `[0, 1]` would map to 0 in the output range `[-180, 180]`.

Clamped.description: Whether to constrain the result within the output range instead of extrapolating beyond its bounds.

Input Max.description: The upper bound of the input range.

Input Min.description: The lower bound of the input range.

Output Max.description: The upper bound of the output range.

Output Min.description: The lower bound of the output range.

Value.description: The value to be mapped between ranges.

math_nodes::RemapNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.remapnode

math_nodes::RgbaToColorNode.description: Constructs a color value from red, green, blue, and alpha components given as numbers from 0 to 1.
math_nodes::RgbaToColorNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.rgbatocolornode

math_nodes::RootNode.description:
The `n`th root operation (`√`) calculates the inverse of exponentiation. Square root inverts squaring, cube root inverts cubing, and so on.

This is equivalent to raising the number to the power of `1/n`. With vec2 inputs, this applies separately to the X and Y components.

Degree.description:
The degree of the root to be calculated. Square root is 2, cube root is 3, and so on.
Degrees 0 or less are invalid and will produce an output of 0.

Radicand.description: The number inside the radical for which the `n`th root is calculated.

math_nodes::RootNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.rootnode

math_nodes::RoundNode.description:
The rounding function (`round`) maps an input value to its nearest whole number. Halfway values are rounded away from zero.

With a vec2 input, this applies separately to the X and Y components.

Value.description: The number to be rounded to the nearest whole number.

math_nodes::RoundNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.roundnode

math_nodes::SignNode.description:
The sign function (`sign`) reports whether an input value is positive (1), negative (-1), or zero (0).

With a vec2 input, this applies separately to the X and Y components.

Value.description: The number whose sign is checked.

math_nodes::SignNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.signnode

math_nodes::SineInverseNode.description: The inverse sine trigonometric function (`asin`) calculates the angle whose sine is the input value.

Radians.description: Whether the resulting angle should be given in as radians instead of degrees.

Value.description: The given value for which the angle is calculated. Must be in the domain `[-1, 1]` (it will be clamped to -1 or 1 otherwise).

math_nodes::SineInverseNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.sineinversenode

math_nodes::SineNode.description:
The sine trigonometric function (`sin`) calculates the ratio of the angle's opposite side length to its hypotenuse length.

With a vec2 input, this applies separately to the X and Y components.

Radians.description: Whether the given angle should be interpreted as radians instead of degrees.

math_nodes::SineNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.sinenode

math_nodes::StringToColorNode.description: Constructs a color value from a CSS color string. Accepts hex (`#RRGGBB`, `#RRGGBBAA`, plus bare and shorthand variants), CSS named colors (like `red`), and functional notations (`rgb(...)`, `hsl(...)`, etc.). Invalid inputs produce a transparent color.

math_nodes::SubtractNode.description: The subtraction operation (`-`) calculates the difference between two scalar numbers or vec2s.

Minuend.description: The left-hand side of the subtraction operation.

Subtrahend.description: The right-hand side of the subtraction operation.

math_nodes::SubtractNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.subtractnode

math_nodes::SumNode.description: Adds together all the numbers in the input list, producing their total.
math_nodes::SumNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.sumnode

math_nodes::SwitchNode.description: Evaluates either the "If True" or "If False" input branch based on whether the input condition is true or false.
math_nodes::SwitchNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.switchnode

math_nodes::TangentInverseNode.description:
The inverse tangent trigonometric function (`atan` or `atan2`, depending on input type) calculates:
`atan`: the angle whose tangent is the input scalar number.
`atan2`: the angle of a ray from the origin to the input vec2.

The resulting angle is always in the range `[-90°, 90°]` or, in radians, `[-π/2, π/2]`.

Radians.description: Whether the resulting angle should be given in as radians instead of degrees.

Value.description: The given value for which the angle is calculated.

math_nodes::TangentInverseNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.tangentinversenode

math_nodes::TangentNode.description:
The tangent trigonometric function (`tan`) calculates the ratio of the angle's opposite side length to its adjacent side length.

With a vec2 input, this applies separately to the X and Y components.

Radians.description: Whether the given angle should be interpreted as radians instead of degrees.

math_nodes::TangentNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.tangentnode

math_nodes::Vec2ValueNode.description: Constructs a vec2 value, a two-dimensional quantity which may be set to any XY pair.
math_nodes::Vec2ValueNode.name: node.type.math_nodes.vec2valuenode

path_bool_nodes::BooleanOperationNode.description: Combines the geometric forms of one or more closed paths into a new vector path that results from cutting or joining the paths by the chosen method.

Content.description: The `List` of vector paths to perform the boolean operation on. Nested `List`s are automatically flattened.

Operation.description:
Which boolean operation to perform on the paths.

Union combines all paths while cutting out overlapping areas (even the interiors of a single path).
Subtraction cuts overlapping areas out from the last (Subtract Front) or first (Subtract Back) path.
Intersection cuts away all but the overlapping areas shared by every path.

path_bool_nodes::BooleanOperationNode.name: node.type.path_bool_nodes.booleanoperationnode

raster_nodes::adjustments::PointsToTrans.description: Builds a transfer curve from a `Vec2[]` of control points, each mapping the input value at its x to the output value at its y. A smooth spline runs through them, holding the outermost points' values beyond them.

raster_nodes::adjustments::PointsToTrans.name: node.type.raster_nodes.adjustments.pointstotransfercurvenode

raster_nodes::filter::BlurNode.description: Blurs the image with a Gaussian or box blur kernel filter.

Box Blur.description: Use a lower-quality box kernel instead of a circular Gaussian kernel. This is faster but produces boxy artifacts.

Gamma.description: Opt to incorrectly apply the filter with color calculations in gamma space for compatibility with the results from other software.

Radius.description: The radius of the blur kernel.

raster_nodes::filter::BlurNode.name: node.type.raster_nodes.filter.blurnode

raster_nodes::filter::MedianFilterNode.description: Applies a median filter to reduce noise while preserving edges.

Radius.description: The radius of the filter kernel. Larger values remove more noise but may blur fine details.

raster_nodes::filter::MedianFilterNode.name: node.type.raster_nodes.filter.medianfilternode

Stencil.description: The stencil to be used for masking.

text_nodes::AsStringNode.description: Type-asserts a value to be a string.
text_nodes::AsStringNode.name: node.type.text_nodes.asstringnode

text_nodes::FormatNumberNode.description: Formats a number as a string with control over decimal places, decimal separator, and thousands grouping.

Decimal Places.description: The amount of digits after the decimal point. The value is rounded to fit. Set to 0 to show only whole numbers.

Decimal Separator.description: The character(s) used as the decimal point.

Fixed Decimals.description: Always show the exact number of decimal places, even if they are trailing zeros.

Number.description: The number to format as a string.

Start at 10,000.description: Don't group 4-digit numbers with a thousands separator (only start grouping at 10,000 and above).

Thousands Separator.description: The character(s) inserted between digit groups.

Use Thousands Separator.description: Whether to group digits with a thousands separator.

text_nodes::FormatNumberNode.name: node.type.text_nodes.formatnumbernode

text_nodes::MapStringNode.description: Iterates over a list of strings, evaluating the mapped operation for each one. Use the **Read String** node to access the current string inside the loop.
text_nodes::MapStringNode.name: node.type.text_nodes.mapstringnode

text_nodes::ReadStringNode.description: Reads the current string from within a **Map String** node's loop.
text_nodes::ReadStringNode.name: node.type.text_nodes.readstringnode

text_nodes::SerializeNode.description: Converts a value to a JSON string representation.
text_nodes::SerializeNode.name: node.type.text_nodes.serializenode

text_nodes::StringCapitalizationNode.description: Converts a string's capitalization style to another of the common upper and lower case patterns, optionally joining words with a chosen separator.

Joiner.description: The string placed between each word.

String.description: The string to have its letter capitalization converted.

Use Joiner.description: Whether to split the string into words and reconnect with the chosen joiner. When disabled, the existing word structure separators are preserved.

text_nodes::StringCapitalizationNode.name: node.type.text_nodes.stringcapitalizationnode

text_nodes::StringContainsNode.description: Checks whether the string contains the given substring. Optionally restricts the match to only the start and/or end of the string.

At End.description: Only match if the substring appears at the end of the string.

At Start.description: Only match if the substring appears at the start of the string.

text_nodes::StringContainsNode.name: node.type.text_nodes.stringcontainsnode

text_nodes::StringEscapeNode.description:
Converts between literal escape sequences and their corresponding control characters within a string.

Unescape: `\n` (newline), `\r` (carriage return), `\t` (tab), `\0` (null), and `\\` (backslash) are converted into the actual special characters.
Escape: the actual special characters are converted back into their escape sequence representations.

Unescape.description: Convert the control characters back into their escape sequence representations.

text_nodes::StringEscapeNode.name: node.type.text_nodes.stringescapenode

text_nodes::StringFindIndexNode.description: Similar to the **String Contains** node, this searches within the input string for the first (or last) occurrence of a substring and returns the index of where that begins, or -1 if not found.

From End.description: Find the start index of the last occurrence instead of the first.

text_nodes::StringFindIndexNode.name: node.type.text_nodes.stringfindindexnode

text_nodes::StringJoinNode.description:
Joins a list of strings together with a separator between each pair. This is the inverse of the **String Split** node.

For example, joining `["a", "b", "c"]` with separator ", " produces "a, b, c".

Separator.description: The text placed between each pair of strings.

Separator Escaping.description:
Whether to convert escape sequences found in the separator into their corresponding characters:
"\n" (newline), "\r" (carriage return), "\t" (tab), "\0" (null), and "\\" (backslash).

Strings.description: The list of strings to join together.

text_nodes::StringJoinNode.name: node.type.text_nodes.stringjoinnode

text_nodes::StringLengthNode.description: Counts the number of characters in a string.
text_nodes::StringLengthNode.name: node.type.text_nodes.stringlengthnode

text_nodes::StringOccurrencesNode.description: Counts the number of occurrences of a substring within the string.

Overlapping.description:
Whether to count overlapping occurrences, using the substring as a sliding window.

text_nodes::StringPadNode.description: Pads the string to a target length by filling with the given repeated substring. If the string already meets or exceeds the target length, it is returned unchanged.

From End.description: Pad at the end of the string instead of the start.

Length.description: The target character length after padding. When "Up To" is set, this length concerns only the portion before (or after) that substring.

Padding.description: The repeated substring used to fill the remaining space. A multi-charcter substring may end partway through its final repetition.

String.description: The string to be padded to a target length.

Up To.description:
Pad only the length of the string encountered before the start of the first (or after the end of the last) occurrence of this substring, if given and present (otherwise the full string is considered).

For example, this can pad numbers with leading zeros to align them before the decimal point.

text_nodes::StringPadNode.name: node.type.text_nodes.stringpadnode

text_nodes::StringRepeatNode.description: Repeats the string a given number of times, optionally with a separator between each repetition.

Count.description: The number of times the string should appear in the output.

Separator.description: The string placed between each repetition.

Separator Escaping.description:
Whether to convert escape sequences found in the separator into their corresponding characters:
"\n" (newline), "\r" (carriage return), "\t" (tab), "\0" (null), and "\\" (backslash).

text_nodes::StringRepeatNode.name: node.type.text_nodes.stringrepeatnode

text_nodes::StringReplaceNode.description: Replaces all occurrences of "From" with "To" in the input string.

text_nodes::StringReverseNode.description: Reverses the sequence of characters making up the string so it reads back-to-front. ("Backwards text" becomes "txet sdrawkcaB".)
text_nodes::StringReverseNode.name: node.type.text_nodes.stringreversenode

text_nodes::StringSliceNode.description:
Extracts a substring from the input string, starting at "Start" and ending before "End".
